nodes.summary: The decision problem EXACT COVER accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of pairs of a natural number and a list of lists of natural numbers, to an instance of EXACT COVER that is well formed and feasible; bitstrings that do not decode are rejected.
nodes.title: EXACT COVER as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, C)$ of EXACT COVER is feasible when $C$ has a sublist $S$, obtained by deleting some entries of $C$, such that for every natural number $x < n$ there is exactly one list that occurs in $S$ and contains $x$.
nodes.title: Feasible EXACT COVER instances

nodes.summary: An instance of EXACT COVER is a pair $(n, C)$ of a natural number $n$, the size of the universe $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, and a finite list $C$ of finite lists of natural numbers, the candidate subsets. That each entry of $C$ lists distinct elements of the universe is required by well-formedness, not by the type of instances.
nodes.title: Instances of EXACT COVER

nodes.summary: The decision problem EXACT COVER is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to it.
nodes.title: EXACT COVER is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n, C)$ of EXACT COVER is well formed when every entry of $C$ is a list of pairwise distinct natural numbers, each less than $n$.
nodes.title: Well-formed EXACT COVER instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
